name: MONA
rootCause: reward-farming / BurnAddress accounting exploit!. Lost: ~60.95K USDT

descriptions.text: reward-farming / BurnAddress accounting exploit!. Lost: ~60.95K USDT

MONA's node-staking vault (LisaVault) paid out a fixed referral split on every 220 USDT node purchase: 80 USDT to the vault reserve, 20 USDT converted to WBNB, 70 USDT to the Level-1 referrer and 50 USDT to the Level-2 referrer. The vault enforced a one-node-per-address limit, but that limit was trivially bypassed by deploying a fresh helper contract per node. The attacker pre-registered an attacker-controlled L2 referrer, then deployed 25 NodeBuyer proxy contracts that each bound the attack contract as their L1 referrer before buying a node, so the attacker captured both referral tiers (70 + 50 USDT) on each of its own purchases. Combined with an insider component where the vault deployer (who also owned ~100% of the MONA/USDT LP) had that LP redeemed to release ~66,450 USDT, the attack netted ~60,950 USDT. The MONA token's transfer restriction (only burn/join addresses) was worked around by leaving MONA with the owner and routing only USDT to the attacker. On April 14, 2026, attackers exploited the BurnAddress mechanism in the MONA token on BSC via a Deferred LP Burn / reserve manipulation attack. The attacker first farmed 10,000 MONA through 25 fresh accounts, sold 9,900 MONA to create a deferred burn credit, bought out most of the pool's MONA inventory, then triggered BurnAddress.burn() with a zero-value transferFrom to burn MONA directly from the LP and call sync(). This left the MONA/USDT pair with near-zero MONA but almost full USDT reserves. Finally, selling the remaining ~100 MONA drained a large amount of USDT. On April 14, 2026, MONA was exploited on BNB Chain when a flawed deferred burn mechanism allowed an attacker to drain the MONA/USDT liquidity pool, resulting in approximately $60,950 in USDT lost. The exploit relied on delayed LP-token burning that could be triggered at attacker-chosen timing after the reserves had been manipulated. The MONA token’s burn mechanism allowed tokens to be removed from the liquidity pool (LP) through a separate burn step, decoupled from the initial sell.
